questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some A are T.

II. Some T are H.

**Conclusions:**

I. No T is A.

II. No H is T.

III. No A is H.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is given below according to the given information.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a26a379e565cd9f833b274373ebfffdd48b672d148f5b2a6a257233ece819df.png] 

Conclusion:

I. No T is A → **Does not follow **→ (As some A are T and some T are H. So, no T is A is not definitely followed)

II. No H is T → **Does not follow **→ (As some A are T and some T are H. So, no H is T is not definitely followed)

III. No A is H → **Does not follow **→ (As some A are T and some T are H. So no A is H is not definitely followed)

So, Neither conclusion follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**

questions.question: As per Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2022, India ranks at ______ position.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **107th**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• India has been ranked 107th out of 121 countries in the 2022 Global Hunger Index (GHI) released on 14th October 2022.
 
• In 2021, India was ranked 101st out of 116 countries.
 
• India has fared poorer than its neighbors Pakistan (99th), Nepal (81st) and Bangladesh (84th).
 
• The index calculates the hunger levels and malnutrition across the world.
 
• Published by: Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points:__**

 
• This year, the report accessed data from 136 countries but evaluated 121 of them. 
 
• The Global Hunger Index score is calculated on four indicators – undernourishment, child wasting (the share of children under the age of five with low weight for their height), child stunting (children under the age of five with low height for their age) and child mortality (the mortality rate of children under the age of five).
 
• India’s global hunger index score is 29.1, which puts the country in the “serious” category of hunger problems.
 
• In 2021, India's score was 27.5.
 
• Lesser GHI score means better ranking in the index.
 
• Globally, 17 countries, including China, Hungary, Montenegro, Uzbekistan, Russia and Saudi Arabia, shared the top spot.
 
• No country has been placed in the extremely alarming category this year.

questions.question: If tan A = 3/7, then what is the value of cosec A?

Trigonometric identity: cosec² A = 1 + cot² A

**Calculation:**

⇒ cosec² A = 1 + (7/3)²

⇒ cosec² A = 1 + 49/9

**Hence, cosec A = √(58) / 3**

questions.question: A 1800 metres long train crosses a man walking in opposite direction in 10 seconds. If the speed of train is 8 times to the speed of man, then what is the speed of train?

Time taken = 10 seconds,

Ratio of speeds = 8:1

Speed = Distance / Time

questions.question: A man borrows a sum of Rs. 12,000 which amounts to Rs. 13,200 in 2 years on simple interest. What would have been the amount if the rate of interest was doubled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple Interest is directly proportional to the rate of interest when Principal and Time are constant.

Original Simple Interest = Rs. 13,200 − Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 1,200

If the rate of interest is doubled, the Simple Interest will also be doubled.

New Simple Interest = 2 × 1,200 = Rs. 2,400

New Amount = Principal + New Interest = 12,000 + 2,400 = Rs. 14,400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 12,000

Amount in 2 years (A) = Rs. 13,200

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = A − P

I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da3a82cf7318b08ad6307d87c03469ea7a1bef468aa7f1c8d3155d0f1097ca39.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Original Interest = 13,200 − 12,000 = Rs. 1,200

⇒ 1,200 = (12,000 × R × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 1,200 = 240 × R

⇒ R = 1,200 ÷ 240 = 5%

⇒ New Rate = 2 × 5% = 10%

⇒ New Interest = (12,000 × 10 × 2) ÷ 100 = Rs. 2,400

⇒ New Amount = 12,000 + 2,400 = Rs. 14,400

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 14,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportionality in Simple Interest

Simple interest is directly proportional to Principal (P), Rate (R), and Time (T). If any one of these is multiplied by a factor while the others remain constant, the Simple Interest is simply multiplied by the same factor.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the original principal every year, meaning it remains constant per period. In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both the original principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Simple Interest Formula

The formula to calculate simple interest is I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100. The total amount at the end of the time period is the sum of the principal and the interest earned: A = P + I.

**Given:**

Expression = (tan θ − sec θ + 1) / (tan θ + sec θ − 1)

sec² θ − tan² θ = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Replace 1 in the numerator with (sec² θ − tan² θ)

⇒ Numerator = tan θ − sec θ + (sec² θ − tan² θ)

⇒ Numerator = −(sec θ − tan θ) + (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ)

⇒ Numerator = (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ − 1)

⇒ Expression = [(sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ − 1)] / (tan θ + sec θ − 1)

⇒ Expression = sec θ − tan θ = (1 / cos θ) − (sin θ / cos θ)

⇒ Expression = (1 − sin θ) / cos θ

⇒ Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin θ)

⇒ Expression = [(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)] / [cos θ(1 + sin θ)]

⇒ Expression = (1 − sin² θ) / [cos θ(1 + sin θ)] = cos² θ / [cos θ(1 + sin θ)]

⇒ Expression = cos θ / (1 + sin θ)

**∴ The correct answer is cos θ / (1 + sin θ).**
